chunks: Mūsā عليه السلام entered into ihram from the sands of Egypt, and he passed at the broad plain of al-Rawhāʾ among seventy Prophets, upon them were al-Qaṭawāniyyah cloaks, saying: ‘Labbayka, Your servant and the son of Your two servants, labbayka.’

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered the state of ihram for pilgrimage
key_terms.الرَّوْحَاءِ: al-Rawhāʾ, a known location mentioned in the narration
key_terms.الْقَطَوَانِيَّةُ: a type of garment or cloak
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Here I am in devoted response to You

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith portray Prophet Mūsā عليه السلام and earlier Prophets in relation to hajj and talbiyah?
ai.summary: This narration describes Mūsā عليه السلام in a state of ihram and recalls a sacred scene involving seventy Prophets at al-Rawhāʾ. It highlights the continuity of hajj devotion and the humble talbiyah of the Prophets as servants of Allah.
